name: Khia
notes: Miami-bass configuration rather than crunk's, and the difference is structural: `session.halfTime` is **false** and the claps go back to 2 and 4, which is the parent's defining parameter reversed. The rest of the TR-808 kit follows — hissy cymbals as continuous 16ths with the highest `openHat.prob` in this batch (0.36), and 808 tom fills at section ends authored as a `tomHigh`/`tomLow` perc pair. ⛔ The research's sharpest claim is that *the kick and the bass are the same voice*: a tuned, very-long-decay sub carrying the tonic. That is `bass808` with a wide-ish low register and almost no slide, over a kick with `lockTo808` left at 1 — not a `reese_sustain` bassline, which would emit one note per chord and saturate. ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set because the research says a single minor triad or a bare root, no progression. Its chord variety therefore comes from `chordDurationBeats` [2, 16], three `harmonicRhythm` values and a wide `voicing.register`, not from families the record does not play. The melodic content the research names is the call-and-response vocal, so what the melody block writes is the repeating high bell figure that sits beside it. ⚠ `confidence` is low: the research rates the entry medium-low, sources only the Miami-bass lineage and the era, and marks the 96–104 straight band [LOW-CONF]. The inferred parameters are the tempo and the whole kit configuration. ⚠ Fill fingerprint for this batch: `gapProb` 0.06 / `descendProb` 0.32 / `rampJitter` 7. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 40 to 39 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 40 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 1. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts.
